newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: U.S. hiker falls off cliff, dies in Costa Rica.
newsitem.headline: U.S. hiker falls off cliff, dies in Costa Rica.

text.p: Rescuers on Saturday found the body of U.S. Peace Corps volunteer Elizabeth Livingston who disappeared while hiking near the Costa Rican capital of San Jose last month, Costa Rican officials said.
The body of the 48-year-old pre-school teacher was found in rugged hills about seven miles (11 km) southwest of San Jose, Red Cross official Carlos Salas told Reuters.

Judicial Police Chief of Operations Manuel Cabezas told Reuters that Livingston suffered multiple and compound fractures that were "consistent with a fall". Her decomposing body was found at the bottom of a 150 foot (45 metre) cliff.
"Apparently she fell, but we won't have an official cause of death until we get a report from the morgue," he said.
Livingston, a divorced mother of one from Santa Fe, New Mexico, was in the third year of her Peace Corps assignment during which she helped a rural community to set up kindergartens.
An avid hiker, Livingston had told friends she planned to walk to the site where a small plane crashed in 1990, 10 miles (16 km) from San Jose.
She was last seen walking alone on March 27 by a group of hikers, Red Cross chief of operations Guillermo Arroyo told reporters.
